record.name: Wuliangshan Gushu Shou
record.origin: Wuliang Mountain, Jingdong County, Pu'er City, Yunnan, China

paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Wuliang Mountain, in Jingdong County, Pu’er City, Yunnan, pressed in 2019. Before pressing, the leaf was [heaped warm and damp](shou:wet-piling) for a month or two, a method Yunnan’s state factories took into production in 1973.
At seven years the cake has reached the stretch, roughly five to ten years on, in which the [smell of the pile](shou:age-settling) has usually gone.

brewing.text: Ease a piece off the cake along its edge with a pick rather than snapping it. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Ripe tea like this gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, sweet cup with earthy or woody notes, which turns cleaner and rounder once the pile note has faded after five years or so.
